summary:
The Holcombe Rucker Park National Commemorative Site Act (Public Law 118-235, approved January 4, 2025) is a freestanding designation statute that does not amend positive law; it is editorially classified as a note to 54 U.S.C. § 320101. The Act’s primary purpose is to confer a federal commemorative designation on a municipally owned park, while expressly excluding the site from the National Park System and limiting the federal role to permissive cooperative agreements.

Section 1 establishes the short title. Section 2(a) designates Holcombe Rucker Park in Harlem, New York, as the “Holcombe Rucker Park National Commemorative Site” (the “Commemorative Site”). Section 2(b) governs administration and constraints. Section 2(b)(1) authorizes—but does not command—the Secretary of the Interior to enter into cooperative agreements with appropriate public or private entities, specifically including the Mayor of New York City or the Mayor’s designee, for interpretive and educational purposes related to the Commemorative Site. Permitted activities under such agreements include installing a plaque, interpretive exhibit, or other marker, conditioned upon obtaining the written consent of the owner of the Commemorative Site, to memorialize the achievements of Holcombe Rucker and recognize the park’s historic role in the development of basketball. Section 2(b)(2) provides that the Commemorative Site shall not be a unit of the National Park System. Section 2(b)(3) sets out three limitations: nothing in the Act (A) authorizes the Secretary to interfere with private property rights, local zoning ordinances, or land-use plans of the State of New York or its political subdivisions, including prohibiting any actions a property owner (including the site owner) may otherwise take with respect to their property; (B) affects the administration of the Commemorative Site by New York City or the State of New York; or (C) authorizes the Secretary to acquire land or interests in land through condemnation or otherwise.

The Act contains no appropriation; the cooperative-agreement authority is a discretionary authorization subject to the availability of funds. No sunset or termination clause is included. The designation and authorities took effect upon enactment.
